en: The Philippines is an archipelago consisting of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main geographical regions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from its source to its mouth.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers during the wet season.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is a highly active volcano in the Philippines, with its main crater measuring only two kilometers across and sitting entirely within a lake.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the deepest point in the Philippine Sea, plunging to 10,540 meters below sea level.
The tamaraw is a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, standing only about one meter tall at the shoulder and weighing up to 300 kilograms.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an underground waterway spanning 8.2 kilometers that flows directly into the sea, making it one of the longest navigable underground rivers.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones per year, with the official typhoon season typically lasting from June to November.
The total land area of the Philippines is approximately 300,000 square kilometers, which is roughly equivalent to the size of the US state of Arizona.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering an area of 109,965 square kilometers, which accounts for about one-third of the country's total landmass.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park protects 97,030 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the Sulu Sea and is home to over 600 fish and coral species.
